# Source Generators

## GeneratedRegex (.NET 7+, C# 11+)

Always prefer `[GeneratedRegex]` over `new Regex(...)` or `Regex.IsMatch(...)`.

| `new Regex(...)` | `[GeneratedRegex]` |
|-------------------|--------------------|
| Compiled at runtime | Compiled at build time |
| Allocates on first use | Zero allocation after startup |
| No Roslyn diagnostics | Pattern errors are compile errors |

```csharp
using System.Text.RegularExpressions;

public partial class Validator
{
    // partial method — implementation generated by compiler
    [GeneratedRegex(@"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$", RegexOptions.None, matchTimeoutMilliseconds: 1000)]
    private static partial Regex DatePattern();

    public bool IsValidDate(string input) => DatePattern().IsMatch(input);
}
```

Rules:
- The class must be `partial`
- The method must be `static partial` returning `Regex`
- Always set `matchTimeoutMilliseconds` to a positive value (prevents ReDoS)
- Use `RegexOptions.IgnoreCase`, `RegexOptions.Multiline` etc. as flags, not inline `(?i)`

For file-level or top-level usage, put the `partial` method in a `partial class` alongside the consumer, or in a dedicated `static partial class Patterns`.

```csharp
// Dedicated patterns class
internal static partial class Patterns
{
    [GeneratedRegex(@"\b[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}\b",
        RegexOptions.IgnoreCase, matchTimeoutMilliseconds: 1000)]
    internal static partial Regex Email();

    [GeneratedRegex(@"^\+?[1-9]\d{1,14}$", matchTimeoutMilliseconds: 1000)]
    internal static partial Regex PhoneE164();
}
```

## LoggerMessage (.NET 6+)

Always prefer `[LoggerMessage]` over `_logger.LogInformation(...)` in production code.

| `_logger.LogInformation(...)` | `[LoggerMessage]` |
|-------------------------------|-------------------|
| Allocates `object[]` for params | Zero allocation |
| Evaluates args even when level disabled | Args only evaluated if enabled |
| No event ID enforcement | Event ID explicit |

```csharp
public partial class OrderService(ILogger<OrderService> logger)
{
    // partial method — implementation generated by compiler
    [LoggerMessage(EventId = 1001, Level = LogLevel.Information,
        Message = "Order {OrderId} placed by {UserId}")]
    private partial void LogOrderPlaced(int orderId, string userId);

    [LoggerMessage(EventId = 1002, Level = LogLevel.Warning,
        Message = "Order {OrderId} payment failed: {Reason}")]
    private partial void LogPaymentFailed(int orderId, string reason);

    [LoggerMessage(EventId = 1003, Level = LogLevel.Error,
        Message = "Unhandled error processing order {OrderId}")]
    private partial void LogOrderError(int orderId, Exception ex);

    public async Task PlaceOrderAsync(Order order)
    {
        LogOrderPlaced(order.Id, order.UserId);
        // ...
    }
}
```

Rules:
- The class must be `partial`
- The method must be `partial` (static or instance); use instance to capture `ILogger` via primary ctor
- Assign a unique, stable `EventId` per log message
- Exception parameters must be named `exception` or typed as `Exception` — placed last
- Message template placeholders `{Name}` become structured log properties
- Use `LogLevel.Debug` / `LogLevel.Trace` for high-frequency diagnostics to avoid overhead when disabled

```csharp
// Static variant — pass ILogger explicitly
public static partial class Log
{
    [LoggerMessage(EventId = 2001, Level = LogLevel.Debug,
        Message = "Cache miss for key {Key}")]
    public static partial void CacheMiss(ILogger logger, string key);
}

// Call site
Log.CacheMiss(_logger, cacheKey);
```
